title: Iridescent Stack — Frosted Mesh Launch
description: Three-plus frosted cards fan across an iridescent purple-to-cyan mesh gradient at staggered rotations, purpose-built for SaaS 'what shipped' recaps and feature matrices that need to feel like a Stripe Sessions keynote moment.
philosophy: This template exists for the moment after the work is done — when the product team finally gets to show the world what shipped. It refuses flat backgrounds and single linear ramps in favor of layered mesh depth that mirrors the complexity of the systems on display. Rotated card stacks signal confident, organized energy; the refraction and inner-shadow borders keep the aesthetic premium without veering into decoration for its own sake. Built for technical and design-literate audiences who know that beauty and engineering are not opposites.
goodFor: SaaS 'what shipped' recap and changelog slides
Feature matrix comparisons across 3–5 product tiers
Product launch keynote hero and transition sections
Developer conference talks in the style of Stripe Sessions or Linear launches
avoidFor: Chart-heavy quarterly business reviews requiring data legibility above all
Conservative corporate board decks with neutral aesthetic requirements
Slides carrying dense long-form copy or multi-paragraph text blocks
author: harness

examples.promptCore: Opening keynote energy — the moment the lights dim and the product finally gets to speak. An iridescent mesh field transitions from deep violet to luminous cyan behind a confident fan of frosted glass cards, each rotated at a slightly different angle as if freshly dealt. Compositional weight is deliberately asymmetric: typographic authority commands the left while the refracting card stack breathes and glows on the right. Every layer should feel physically deep and lit from within — premium without decoration, technical without coldness, never flat.

examples.layoutNotes: Full-bleed iridescent mesh background with no header band and an ~8% outer margin on all sides. A 12-column grid anchors the deck title and subtitle flush-left in columns 1–7, vertically centered with a slight upward bias to create visual lift. Three frosted glass cards fan across columns 6–12 at staggered clockwise rotations, with the rearmost card partially bleeding off the right edge to reinforce physical depth. A minimal deck tag or session label sits bottom-left; no footer rule or page-number band on this hero slide.

examples.promptCore: Frosted-glass cards fan across a deep iridescent mesh gradient pulsing from violet through cyan, each catching refracted light at its rotated edge — a triumphant product-reveal moment. The composition is asymmetric and kinetic, confident and organized, evoking the visual language of a Stripe Sessions or Linear changelog keynote. Mood is premium-engineered: technical precision married to visual drama, where layered depth signals systemic complexity rather than decoration. Avoid symmetrical card arrangements, flat static layouts, or any compositional softness that would dilute the launch-moment intensity.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with a 6% outer gutter on all sides; slide title anchors top-left in cols 1–8, separated from the card stack by a hairline rule. Three frosted cards occupy cols 3–12 in the main content zone, each rotated at a progressively greater clockwise offset to form a fanned-hand composition. Each card contains a feature label at its top edge, a one-line descriptor below, and an optional status badge or icon in its upper corner. Page number sits bottom-right, clear of the card stack footprint.
